questions.solution:
Total cases will be  5C4×4!

Now favourable cases for 2fb=fc+fd-fa will be,

Case (I) if fb=1 then fc, fd, fa can take the value 3,4,5 & 4,3,5 respectively

Case (II) if fb=2 then fc, fd, fa can take value 3,5,4 & 5,3,4 respectively

Case (III) if fb=3 then fc, fd, fa can take value 2,5,1 & 5,2,1 respectively

So total favourable case will be 6

So probability=favourable casestotal outcomes=65×4!=120

questions.q: In a binomial distribution <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>)</mo></math>, the sum and product of the mean & variance are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn></math> respectively, then find <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>6</mn><mo>(</mo><mi>n</mi><mo>+</mo><mi>p</mi><mo>-</mo><mi>q</mi><mo>)</mo></math> is equal to :-
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
For the binomial distribution B(n, p),

Mean =np and Variance =npq

Sum of mean and variance =np+npq=5

⇒np(1+q)=5

⇒n2p2(1+q)2=25     ....(1)

Product of mean and variance =np.npq=6

⇒n2p2q=6      ....(2)

Put the value of n2p2 from equation (2) into equation (1):

6q(1+q)2=25

⇒6q2+12q+6=25q

⇒6q2-13q+6=0

⇒(3q-2)(2q-3)=0

⇒q=23, 32 where q=23 accepted

∴ p=13⇒n·13+n·13·23=5

⇒3n+2n9=5

⇒n=9

Therefore,

6(n+p-q)=69+13-23=52

questions.q: The probability that a randomly chosen <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn></math>- digit number is made from exactly two digits is :
questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.solution:
Total number of five-digit numbers are 9104.

Case I : Choosing two non-zero digits i.e. in C29 ways.

So, number of five-digit numbers containing both digits =25-2.

Case II : Choose one non-zero and one zero as digit i.e. in C19 ways.

So, number of five-digit numbers containing one non-zero and one zero both =24-1.

So, favourable number of ways =C2925-2+C1924-1=3630+915=1080+135=1215

Thus, required probability =12159×104=135104.

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\mathrm{k}}=1+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3}{3^2}+\frac{4}{3^3}+$ ...(i)
$\frac{1}{3 \mathrm{k}}=\frac{1}{3}+\frac{2}{3^2}+\frac{3}{3^3}+\ldots$ ...(ii)

$\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \mathrm{k}=\frac{4}{9} \\ & \mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x} \geq 3)=1-\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}=0)-\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}=1)-\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{x}=2) \\ & =1-\mathrm{k}\left(1+\frac{2}{3}+\frac{3}{9}\right)=\frac{1}{9}\end{aligned}$
